identity.name: enrich_heritage
identity.description: Single-pass ENRICHER: spatial-joins parcels.geom against heritage_properties (Part IV individual) and heritage_districts (Part V HCD) and writes the designation flag + type + date + dataset lineage stamp in ONE set-based join UPDATE, scoped to eligible parcels (geom non-null, non-empty, valid) whose lineage stamp is stale against the current combined heritage version (H-A1 (a) — Layer-2 subsumes the pre-conversion #418 Layer-1 cheap-COUNT early return). The Layer-1 mechanism is RETIRED as a mechanism (deviations[]) — the ENRICHER runner has no gated-skip branch by design — its OBSERVABLE is preserved: the Layer-2 scope predicate already yields a 0-row write in steady state, and parcels_heritage_enrich_skipped is re-derived from the write count.

why_lock.text: DEC-A — sibling of load_heritage=61; 62 verified free. Spec 61 :441/:852/:934 still print 63 and are corrected by this conversion's spec diff (deferred to cutover); Spec 47 §A.5 :1969 already reads 62. Kept textually per Spec 122 §5.4 so the registry loop (src/tests/pipeline-advisory-lock.infra.test.ts) stays green across the conversion.

guard_columns_why.text: The verbatim 4-column guard, legacy ENRICH_SQL:257-260. The lineage stamp is INSIDE the guard: like enrich_ravines' and unlike geocode_permits' run-clock geocoded_at, it is a content hash of the two source datasets, constant across runs against the same load, so including it is what makes a second run write 0 rows instead of re-stamping 486,514 parcels.

write_discipline.scope: p.geom IS NOT NULL AND NOT ST_IsEmpty(p.geom) AND ST_IsValid(p.geom) AND p.heritage_dataset_version_when_enriched IS DISTINCT FROM $2

invalidates.when: load-parcels.js's ON CONFLICT nulls the stamp via a CASE gated ONLY on parcels.geometry::jsonb IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.geometry::jsonb (DEC-FENCE2, anchor `heritage_dataset_version_when_enriched = CASE`) — app code, NOT migration 242's trigger, which deliberately covers only massing/zoning. A load_heritage source_dataset_version bump on EITHER dataset stales every parcel, because the stamp is the two versions concatenated.

why.text: Exactly one write statement per invocation, in every mode and on every chain — the H-A1(a) Layer-2 WITH...UPDATE, executed through ctx.joinUpdate. There is no batching beyond the scope predicate itself.

staleness.scope: eligible parcels (geom non-null, non-empty, valid) whose heritage_dataset_version_when_enriched IS DISTINCT FROM `<register>|<districts>` from the producer's most recent completed run

why.text: The ST_Intersects containment joins (Part IV point-in-parcel, Part V polygon-in-parcel) are non-viable without PostGIS. Ported verbatim from the legacy assertPreconditions (DEC-F, §3.10).
Migration 170 — levenshtein() is the Part IV tiebreak when a parcel contains more than one Part IV point. Absent, the join fails mid-statement instead of refusing up front.

Output-panel O1 (Guardian, 2026-09-20): the legacy assertPreconditions probed `SELECT 1 FROM pg_proc WHERE proname = 'normalize_address'` (migration 170, introduced e299d26e) BEFORE this conversion — ENRICH_SQL calls normalize_address() twice (the parcel address CTE and the Part IV tiebreak), and the join fails mid-statement with a raw 42883 (function does not exist) instead of a named refusal if it is absent. Dropped undeclared at commit 2; restored here.

Migration 170 — binds the Part IV containment LATERAL (point-in-parcel via ST_Intersects). Without it every parcel seq-scans all 8,824 heritage_properties rows.

on_check_error_why.text: Every declared check reads a count the library already measured in the same run (the coverage/counts SQL in computePostPhase); a check that throws is a compute defect, not an upstream data condition, and must redden the run rather than silently drop its row (the geocode_permits / compute_centroids / enrich_ravines precedent).

why.text: Broken-join FAIL gate: a hard zero means the spatial join matched NOTHING (wrong SRID / unbound GIST / a broken join), distinct from a legitimately-small heritage subset. Ported exactly: 0 -> FAIL, >=1 -> PASS. Measured live 2026-09-20: 9,958.

EH-D2 (declared diff, Spec 124 §7 rung (b)): the legacy's WARN was conditional on partIvSource > 0; this port's bound is unconditional 0 -> WARN, >=1 -> PASS. The two differ only when the register loads zero part_iv points, where the ported form is LOUDER (WARN vs INFO), never quieter. Measured live 2026-09-20: 1,217.
Ported by name. Measured live 2026-09-20: 8,741.
Ported by name. Measured live 2026-09-20: 1,557.

why.text: R-AD 3-tier. Unit note, load-bearing: the legacy compared a FRACTION (0.15/0.30) against a fraction while REPORTING a PERCENTAGE (round(frac*1000)/10); the converted check compares the reported value, so the seeds are 15/30, not 0.15/0.30. Comparison semantics identical; the INFO->PASS tier rename is a declared Class A diff. Measured live 2026-09-20: 10.4%.

WARN-on->0 would force a perpetual-WARN verdict (alert fatigue) — the legacy's own explicit reasoning, preserved as the declared exception to Rule 10's R-H addendum. Measured live 2026-09-20: 16.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*)::int FROM parcels WHERE is_heritage_designated AND heritage_designation_type IS NULL

why.text: Half of the whole semantic of new_designated = (hcd_id IS NOT NULL OR hp_id IS NOT NULL): a flagged parcel must carry a non-null type. A port error in the CASE breaks this silently while every count-row stays green. MEASURED 0 across all 486,530 parcels, 2026-09-20.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*)::int FROM parcels WHERE NOT is_heritage_designated AND heritage_designation_type IS NOT NULL

why.text: The inverse direction of the same semantic: an unflagged parcel must never carry a type. MEASURED 0 across all 486,530 parcels, 2026-09-20.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*)::int FROM parcels WHERE heritage_designation_date IS NOT NULL AND heritage_designation_type IS NULL

why.text: A date can only be set alongside a type — both come from the same winning side of the CASE. MEASURED 0, 2026-09-20.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*)::int FROM parcels WHERE heritage_designation_type = 'part_iv_individual' AND heritage_designation_date IS NULL

why.text: Scoped to Part IV only — the Part V arm legitimately carries 1,820 null dates (4 of 29 heritage_districts rows have a NULL designated_date, §7). Every heritage_properties Part IV row has a non-null designated_date, so a Part IV parcel with a null date is a port error, not a source-data fact. MEASURED 0, 2026-09-20.

plausibility.sql: SELECT (100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE is_heritage_designated) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0))::float FROM parcels
plausibility.retighten_when: never — a city-wide ceiling on how much of the parcel fabric can plausibly be heritage-designated, not a convergence target. Measured live 2.047%.

why.text: A join that started over-matching (SRID drift, unbound GIST returning a Cartesian product) would spike this share; a ceiling well above the measured value catches the regression class without ever nearing the legitimate value.

plausibility.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE is_heritage_designated)::float FROM parcels
plausibility.retighten_when: never — the mirror-image floor of heritage_designated_share_max_pct. A ceiling-only set is blind to a collapse: a join that silently matched 3% of what it should would satisfy every existing row (parcels_heritage_designated_count only FAILs at exactly 0). Measured live 9,958.

why.text: Reality-Check plan-altitude demand (§7, the enrich_ravines output-panel O4 precedent applied at plan altitude here rather than discovered at output): a floor far below the measured count but far above zero, catching a partial-collapse regression neither the FAIL-at-0 gate nor the share ceiling can see.

plausibility.sql: SELECT GREATEST(0, (SELECT count(*) FROM parcels WHERE heritage_designation_type = 'part_iv_individual') - (SELECT count(*) FROM heritage_properties WHERE status = 'part_iv'))::float
plausibility.retighten_when: never — a structural containment-arithmetic bound: containment assigns at most one parcel per source point, so parcels-with-Part-IV can never exceed source Part IV points. Measured 1,217 <= 1,557 => 0.

why.text: A LATERAL join bug that fanned out (returned more than one match per point) would break this identity while every per-metric count still looks locally plausible.

deviations.from: the pre-conversion #418 Layer-1 cheap-COUNT early return (a full transaction-avoidance branch, evaluated before opening any transaction)

why.text: F9 / H-A1 (a), RULED (operator, 2026-09-20) — RETIRED as a MECHANISM, knowingly. The ENRICHER runner has no gated-skip branch by design. A Layer-2 predicate carrying the IDENTICAL eligibility countStale applied is ported into parcel_c, so Layer-2 SUBSUMES Layer-1: a zero-stale run is already a 0-row write, and parcels_heritage_enrich_skipped is RE-DERIVED from updated === 0 rather than from the retired branch. Value-equivalence for rows in scope is proven by the §4.5 NULL-stamped cohort differential, not the (refuted) forced-FULL instrument. What this knowingly gives up is declared in limitations[] (FOLD-I5).

deviations.from: the legacy's Part-IV WARN gate, conditional on partIvSource > 0

why.text: EH-D2 — the ported bound is unconditional (0 -> WARN, >=1 -> PASS). The two forms differ only when the register loads zero part_iv points, where the ported form is louder (WARN vs INFO), never quieter. Adjudicated as a declared check/audit-row diff (Spec 124 §7 rung (b)), not re-implemented as a two-input rule in compute.

limitations.what: EH-D1 — emitMeta declared reads {parcels:['id','geom','addr_num_normalized','street_name_normalized','street_type_normalized']} but the SQL reads more: parcels.heritage_dataset_version_when_enriched (scope + guard), parcels.is_heritage_designated/heritage_designation_type/heritage_designation_date (the guard), heritage_properties.id, heritage_districts.id, plus pipeline_runs.records_meta (the §9 contract). The descriptor's inputs.reads.tables[] above declares the WIDENED, honest read set.
limitations.measured: grep of ENRICH_SQL + readHeritageContract against the pre-conversion emitMeta call, 2026-09-20.

limitations.what: RV-L2 class — guards.srid and guards.empty_source are DECLARATIVE, not runner-enforced preconditions. scripts/lib/step/index.js has zero references to either field; the real L14/SRID enforcement is folded into the contract_read hook (readHeritageContract), which is guaranteed to run pre-transaction on every invocation.
limitations.measured: grep -n 'empty_source|guards.srid' scripts/lib/step/index.js — zero hits, 2026-09-20 (same measurement as enrich_ravines' RV-L2).

limitations.what: RV-L3 class — this step's contract_read hook does not need config threading (unlike enrich_ravines, readHeritageContract has no numeric threshold at all: every gate is !x, === false, or > 0), so the RV-L3 gap does not apply here. Cross-referenced, not re-opened.
limitations.measured: read of readHeritageContract, 2026-09-20 — no comparison against a config value anywhere in the hook.

limitations.what: EH-D3 — spec-citation drift found while grounding: Spec 61's cited DEC-E/DEC-F/DEC-H ids do not exist in Spec 61 (inherited from the Spec 59 ravines port); the script's '§3.10 SRID guard' comment points at Spec 61 :370 ('Edge cases'), which has no SRID clause (the real clause is Spec 59 :383); L14 is spec'd for the loader (61:67) while the enrich-side non-empty HALT is L23 step 4 (61:645); L24 (61:77) names enrich-permits.js, not this script. Recorded here; the spec-text correction rides commit 3 (cutover) per Spec 123's rule that a spec-only fix does not belong in a behaviour-differential commit.
limitations.measured: cross-read of docs/specs/01-pipeline/61_source_heritage_properties.md against scripts/enrich-heritage.js's own comments, 2026-09-20.

limitations.what: Output-panel O3 (Observability, 2026-09-20) — records_meta.heritage_designated_by_zone[].parcels sums to ALL 486,530 parcels (COALESCE(zoning_class,'(null)') has no eligibility filter), NOT eligible_parcels_scanned (486,514) — the 16 invalid-geom parcels ARE counted in some zone bucket's .parcels total even though they can never be designated. Only the designated-sum identity is claimed and asserted (sum of buckets.designated == parcels_heritage_designated_count): the .parcels totals are population context only, not a second eligibility-scoped count.
limitations.measured: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM parcels = 486530 vs the eligible-only 486514 (16 invalid-geom), 2026-09-20.

limitations.what: FOLD-I5 — under H-A1 (a), two input-change classes no longer re-stale on their own: (1) an enrich_heritage_address_levenshtein_threshold change only affects which Part IV point wins inside a multi-point parcel (MEASURED: 94 multi-Part-IV-point parcels holding 272 points, max 15 in one parcel, out of 1,217 parcels with any Part IV point — the only field that can move is heritage_designation_date, on at most 94 parcels); (2) an address-only parcel edit (addr_num_normalized/street_name_normalized/street_type_normalized rewritten with an unchanged geometry) has the same 94-parcel bound via the tiebreak's norm_addr side. The legacy healed both BY ACCIDENT (no Layer-2 meant every stale>0 run re-evaluated all 486,514 parcels) — a side effect of the missing predicate, not a designed guarantee. Remedy: ENRICH_HERITAGE_FORCE_FULL (retained, load-bearing). The per-row/threshold-aware invalidation idea is filed to review_followups.md at cutover, not built here.
limitations.measured: WITH m AS (SELECT p.id, COUNT(*) n FROM parcels p JOIN heritage_properties hp ON hp.status='part_iv' AND ST_Intersects(p.geom,hp.geom) WHERE <eligibility> GROUP BY p.id) SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE n>1), SUM(n) FILTER (WHERE n>1), MAX(n), COUNT(*) FROM m — run live 2026-09-20.

recovery.reset: No TRUNCATE/rebuild mechanism and none is needed — a plain re-run re-evaluates every eligible parcel whose stamp disagrees with the current heritage version (staleness.scope) and the IS DISTINCT FROM 4-column guard makes an unnecessary re-stamp cheap. Nulling parcels.heritage_dataset_version_when_enriched by hand for a scoped set of parcels IS a valid targeted reset.

interrupted_why.text: The single write target sits inside ONE shared transaction (execution.txn_scope 'step', the phase's own txn 'shared'), so a run killed mid-statement leaves parcels exactly as it found them — no half-written state (proven by the new enrich-heritage-kill-mid-run.db.test.ts, pg_cancel_backend, not a process kill). force_full_on_next_run is accurate, not a resumption claim: runEnrichPhase folds staleness.detectInterruptedRetraction into full before any pass runs, and because this step's scope predicate re-admits every stale parcel unconditionally on every run, the next run does a full pass over whatever is still stale whether or not the prior run was interrupted.

before_image_why.text: recovery.before_image applies to a retraction (outputs.writes[].retract != 'none'); this step's sole write target declares retract:'none' — it only ever stamps a value, never clears one to NULL.

why.text: A4 ruling (operator, applied per the enrich_parcels/enrich_ravines ENRICHER precedent): declares the scanned population. matched.compute.<name> resolves while a bare compute.* resolves NULL for every ENRICHER.

This step INSERTs nothing — the sole write target is an UPDATE, and class N's own executor structurally refuses any statement text containing INSERT INTO or ON CONFLICT. Declared as a finite literal 0 rather than omitted, because an omitted source resolves null and null reads as 'not counted'.

COUNTER-ROOT: write.targetKey(0) returns 'e1' — the rowCount of the sole declared write target, one-to-one with the legacy's `updated` counter. RV-D4's seamOwned guard has landed (scripts/lib/step/index.js), so the pass returns { updated, sourceDatasetVersion } with no key-name workaround.

Spec 61 §12.3a seeds a radius-match parameter (heritage_point_match_radius_m) that live validation superseded: Part IV switched from ST_DWithin(radius) to ST_Intersects containment (the ST_DWithin form over-matched 4x — 6,217 parcels vs 1,549 source points). The legacy ConfigSchema comment states this was 'left out of the schema rather than declared-and-ignored'; declaring it retired here is the honest, checker-visible form of the same fact.

The heritage_join phase ran (whether or not its scope was empty) and every blocking check met its PASS bound.

The phase ran and at least one non-blocking check (e.g. parcels_part_iv_count, heritage_points_no_parcel_match's WARN tier, or a plausibility row) is below PASS. Row-derived, never a parallel boolean.

readHeritageContract threw — the §9 producer-protocol HALT (missing/failed/stale producer, missing sub-block, zero feature_count, drift_check_passed=false, empty lineage) OR the L14 empty-source HALT OR the SRID=4326 assertion, all folded into this ONE pre-transaction hook. PRESERVED: the legacy also halts before any transaction opens for every one of these conditions.
